classification.difficultyReason: Recognise equal perpendicular corner offsets, apply Pythagoras twice and combine the explicitly supplied collinear length relation with tangent radii. The final linear surd equation and rationalisation follow those guided links without an unsignposted geometric construction.

content.prompt:
A circle of radius $10$ cm and centre $O$ is placed inside the square $ABCD$ of side length $20$ cm. A small circle with centre $G$ is placed between a corner of the square and the circle so that it touches the circle and the two sides of the square.

Note: You may assume that the points $O$, $G$ and $A$ lie on the same line.

spec.description: Unfilled square with an inscribed circle and a smaller circle tangent to the top and left sides at corner A and externally tangent to the large circle. Both centres are marked. No joining line is drawn. Ordinary source blue outlines and red centre markers use house black.
spec.mathematics: Square side 20 cm; large radius 10 cm. In drawing units the square side is 4, large radius is 2 and small radius is 6-4sqrt(2), ensuring exact tangency. A, G and O are collinear.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and labels are visible; the small radius is not labelled.

answer.worked:
The centre $O$ is $10$ cm from each side of the square. By Pythagoras,
$$\begin{align*}OA^2&=10^2+10^2\\OA^2&=200\\OA&=\sqrt{200}\\OA&=10\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: If the radius of the small circle is $r$ centimetres, find the length of $GA$ in terms of $r$.

answer.worked:
Since the small circle touches both sides at corner $A$, its centre is $r$ centimetres from each side. By Pythagoras,
$$\begin{align*}GA^2&=r^2+r^2\\GA^2&=2r^2\\GA&=r\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

The circles touch externally, so $OG=10+r$ centimetres.
$$\begin{align*}OA&=OG+GA\\OA&=(10+r)+r\sqrt{2}\\OA&=10+r+r\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

Equating the two expressions for $OA$,
$$\begin{align*}10\sqrt{2}&=10+r+r\sqrt{2}\\r(1+\sqrt{2})&=10\sqrt{2}-10\\r&=\frac{10(\sqrt{2}-1)}{\sqrt{2}+1}\\r&=\frac{10(\sqrt{2}-1)^2}{(\sqrt{2}+1)(\sqrt{2}-1)}\\r&=10(3-2\sqrt{2})\\r&=30-20\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
